newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Crash talk hits Kuwait share index in week.
newsitem.headline: Crash talk hits Kuwait share index in week.

text.p: Kuwait's share index lost 40 points to 2,296.6 in a caution-dominated week as investors weighed mixed opinions about a market crash, traders said on Wednesday.
"The week was dominated by uncertainty," said a portfolio manager, echoing views shared by fellow investors. "The market should not be toyed with."

On Saturday some parliamentarians, lashing out at the government's economic policies, warned of a possible market crash. Officials swiftly dismissed this and said the situation was "reassuring", while some economists expected a market correction.
The warnings coincided with a cabinet review on Sunday of the Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) performance, which one dealer said may have given investors a false sign of problems.
Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan has said there was no link between the review and parliamentarians' opinions.
Talk of a crash revived memories of the 1982 collapse of an unofficial bourse that plagued the economy for year with about $20 billion worth of bad debts.

Central Bank Governor Sheikh Salem Abdul-Aziz al-Sabah, in a statement to the official Kuwait News Agency late on Tuesday, voiced discomfort with increased speculation by groups of big investors and gyrating share prices.
Analysts, commenting on fears of a crash, have said some big investors were forming trading pools to drive prices up, and warned of negative effects on small investors.

Fears of a correction emerged late last year as trading value soared above $160 million a day but talk of a crash gained steam when the daily trading value hit $414 million and the index set the new record of 2,354.7 on April 27.

In the week to Wednesday the daily average for value of traded shares fell to 70 million dinars ($327 million) from 99.4 million. Volume eased to a daily average of 237.4 million shares from 345 million, KSE figures show.
Investment firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 141.6 million dinars, followed by real estate firms with 75 million and banks with 56 million.
United Realty, Kuwait Real Estate, Investment Projects, National Investment, Real Estate Bank and Gulf Bank were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
